## Solution

Make the substitution $u = x/y$ in the inner integral. For fixed $y > 0$, set $x = uy$, $dx = y\,du$; as $x$ ranges over $(0,\infty)$, so does $u$. Then

$$
\frac{n}{x}\sin\!\left(\frac{x}{ny}\right)e^{-x/y - y}\,dx
= \frac{n}{uy}\sin\!\left(\frac{u}{n}\right)e^{-u-y}\cdot y\,du
= \frac{n}{u}\sin\!\left(\frac{u}{n}\right)e^{-u-y}\,du.
$$

The double integral therefore separates:

$$
I_n = \int_0^\infty\!\int_0^\infty \frac{n}{u}\sin\!\left(\frac{u}{n}\right)e^{-u-y}\,du\,dy
= \left(\int_0^\infty e^{-y}\,dy\right)\!\left(\int_0^\infty \frac{n}{u}\sin\!\left(\frac{u}{n}\right)e^{-u}\,du\right).
$$

The $y$-integral equals $1$, so

$$
I_n = \int_0^\infty \frac{n}{u}\sin\!\left(\frac{u}{n}\right)e^{-u}\,du.
$$

**Pointwise limit.** For every fixed $u > 0$,

$$
\frac{n}{u}\sin\!\left(\frac{u}{n}\right) = \frac{\sin(u/n)}{u/n} \xrightarrow{n\to\infty} 1.
$$

**Domination.** Using $\sin t \le t$ for $t \ge 0$ with $t = u/n$,

$$
0 \le \frac{n}{u}\sin\!\left(\frac{u}{n}\right) \le \frac{n}{u}\cdot\frac{u}{n} = 1.
$$

Hence the integrand is bounded by $e^{-u}$, which is integrable on $(0,\infty)$. By the dominated convergence theorem,

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty} I_n = \int_0^\infty \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{n}{u}\sin\!\left(\frac{u}{n}\right)e^{-u}\,du = \int_0^\infty e^{-u}\,du = 1.
$$

$$
\boxed{\lim_{n\to\infty} \int_0^\infty\!\!\int_0^\infty \frac{n}{x}\sin\!\left(\frac{x}{ny}\right)e^{-x/y-y}\,dx\,dy = 1.}
$$
